category: RF & Wave Optics III: transient, time-explicit, boundary-element, asymptotic, beam-envelope and transmission-line interfaces, and electromagnetic heating
description: The electromagnetic-wave interfaces beyond the FEM frequency-domain one: Wave Optics variants (ewfd, ewt, teew, ebem), Electromagnetic Waves, Transient/Time Explicit/Boundary Elements/Asymptotic Scattering/Beam Envelopes features, FEM-BEM coupling, the Transmission Line family, Microwave/Laser Heating with their studies, the Wavelength Domain study and the thermal-lensing (ray heating) workflow. Type strings and property names come from COMSOL 6.4 plugin definitions and Application Library models.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain (ewfd)
tools.description: Wave Optics Module version of the full-wave time-harmonic interface (Java type ElectromagneticWavesFrequencyDomain, default tag ewfd). It solves the same curl-curl equation for E as the RF Module's emw interface but is found under Optics > Wave Optics and additionally supports the Wavelength Domain study, so optical models are swept in vacuum wavelength with refractive-index material data. Use it for nanophotonics, plasmonics, gratings, metasurfaces, photonic crystals and short waveguide devices where the structure is a few wavelengths in size.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Optics > Wave Optics > Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain (ewfd). API: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ewfd", "ElectromagneticWavesFrequencyDomain", "geom1"); model.study("std1").create("wave", "Wavelength")

parameters.name: Studies
parameters.description: Wavelength Domain, Frequency Domain, Adaptive Frequency Sweep, Eigenfrequency, Mode Analysis (2D/2D-axi), Boundary Mode Analysis, Frequency Domain Modal, Frequency Domain Source Sweep.

parameters.name: Formulation / components / BackgroundField
parameters.description: Same interface settings as emw (full or scattered field, Gaussian beam or plane-wave background).

parameters.name: Wave-optics-only features
parameters.description: Cross Section Calculation and Polarization domain nodes.

tools.notes: All emw feature nodes (ports, periodic structures, far-field domains, layered conditions) are available with the ewfd prefix, e.g. ewfd.Rorder_0_0, ewfd.normE. Requires the Wave Optics Module; the RF interface is catalogued as 'Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain (emw)'.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Waves, Transient (ewt)
tools.description: Wave Optics Module version of the time-domain vector-potential interface (Java type ElectromagneticWavesTransient, tag ewt), solving the second-order wave equation for the magnetic vector potential A with an implicit time-dependent solver. It is chosen for nonlinear optics (Kerr effect, second-harmonic generation through a remanent-displacement or polarization term), dispersive Drude-Lorentz media and pulse propagation, typically followed by a Time to Frequency FFT to obtain spectra.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Optics > Wave Optics > Electromagnetic Waves, Transient (ewt). API: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ewt", "ElectromagneticWavesTransient", "geom1"); model.study("std1").create("time", "Transient")

parameters.name: Studies
parameters.description: Time Dependent, Time Dependent Modal, Time Dependent with FFT, Eigenfrequency.

parameters.name: components
parameters.description: 2D: threecomponent, outofplane or inplane.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Magnetic vector potential, Quadratic by default.

tools.notes: Feature set equals the RF Module's Electromagnetic Waves, Transient (temw). Time steps must resolve the optical period, so for long linear devices prefer frequency-domain or beam-envelope methods, and for large linear transient problems the time-explicit DG interface.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit (ewte / teew)
tools.description: Time-domain interface that solves Faraday's and Maxwell-Ampere's laws as two first-order equations for E and H with the nodal discontinuous Galerkin method and explicit time stepping, in linear media only. Memory scales with the number of elements rather than a factorized matrix, so it handles electrically large transient problems - wideband RCS, antenna pulses, EMC of large structures, ultrafast optics - that are impractical with the implicit temw/ewt interfaces. Open boundaries use Absorbing Layers (with filtering) or Scattering Boundary Conditions.
tools.usage: RF Module: Radio Frequency > Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit (tag ewte, type ElectromagneticWavesTimeExplicit); Wave Optics Module: Wave Optics > Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit (tag teew, type ElectromagneticWavesDiscontinuousGalerkin). API: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ewte", "ElectromagneticWavesTimeExplicit", "geom1")

parameters.name: Field components solved for (2D/2D-axi)
parameters.description: Full wave (default), E in plane (TM wave) or H in plane (TE wave).

parameters.name: Filter Parameters for Absorbing Layers
parameters.description: alpha, eta_c, s defaults 0.5, 0.1, 4 (advanced options).

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Linear, Quadratic, Cubic (default) or Quartic for E and H.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Wave Equations, Perfect Electric Conductor, Initial Values.

tools.example:
Wideband RCS in one run:
1. Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit with a Background Field (modulated Gaussian pulse).
2. Absorbing Layer around the air domain; Far-Field Domain with Far-Field Calculation.
3. Time Dependent study + Time to Frequency FFT, then plot ewte far-field RCS versus frequency.
Application Library: RF_Module/Scattering_and_RCS/rcs_time_explicit
tools.notes: Physics-controlled mesh: User defined size by default; the Frequency or Wavelength options give lambda0/5 (3D) or lambda0/8 (2D) for quadratic elements (scaled for other orders). The explicit time step is limited by the smallest element (CFL condition), so avoid tiny elements; nonlinear and dispersive materials are not supported (use temw/ewt).

tools.name: Wave Equations (Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Main domain node of the time-explicit interface holding the linear material properties (relative permittivity, relative permeability, electric conductivity, each isotropic or tensor) and the numerical flux settings of the discontinuous Galerkin scheme. The estimate of maximum wave speed sets the explicit time step, the flux type (Lax-Friedrichs or upwind, with central flux as a special case) controls dissipation, and an optional exponential filter stabilizes problems with strongly varying coefficients.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit > Wave Equations 1 (default, tag weqs1). API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewte").feature("weqs1") (type WaveEquations)

parameters.name: Relative permittivity / permeability / conductivity
parameters.description: From material or User defined (Isotropic, Diagonal, Symmetric, Full).

parameters.name: Estimate of maximum wave speed cmax
parameters.description: Used for the stable explicit time step; default c_const (speed of light in vacuum).

parameters.name: Flux type
parameters.description: Lax-Friedrichs (tauE = 0.5/Z, tauH = 0.5*Z by default) or Upwind flux (scaling factor 1; 0 gives central flux).

parameters.name: Filter settings (advanced)
parameters.description: Automatic (alpha 0.5 in absorbing layers, 0.05 elsewhere, eta_c 0.01, s 4), Only use filter on absorbing layers, or User defined.

tools.example:
Dielectric radome illuminated by a pulse: Wave Equations 2 on the radome with epsr = 4.2 from material; keep Lax-Friedrichs flux and automatic filter settings.
Application Library: RF_Module/Scattering_and_RCS/rcs_time_explicit
tools.notes: See 'Theory for the Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit Interface' for the flux formulation and absorbing layers.

tools.name: Electric and Magnetic Current Density (Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Domain sources of the time-explicit interface: Electric Current Density adds Je (A/m^2) to Ampere's law and Magnetic Current Density adds Jm (V/m^2) to Faraday's law. They are used for volumetric time-domain excitations such as a pulsed current sheet, a soft source inside the computational domain or equivalent magnetic sources.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Electric Current Density / Magnetic Current Density. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewte").create("ecu1", "ElectricCurrentDensity", 3); physics("ewte").create("mcu1", "MagneticCurrentDensity", 3)

parameters.name: Electric current density Je
parameters.description: Time-dependent vector expression in A/m^2.

parameters.name: Magnetic current density Jm
parameters.description: Time-dependent vector expression in V/m^2.

tools.example: Pulsed line source in a 2D TM (E in plane) model: Electric Current Density on a thin domain with Je = (0, J0*exp(-((t-t0)/tau)^2)*sin(2*pi*f0*t), 0).
tools.notes: Boundary sources are Surface Current Density and Flux/Source; plane-wave illumination is best done with the Background Field feature.

tools.name: Scattering Boundary Condition (Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: First-order absorbing boundary of the time-explicit interface that specifies the tangential electric and magnetic fields of an outgoing plane wave and can inject an incident wave E0(t). It is a cheap open boundary for waves arriving near normal incidence; for oblique or evanescent content use Absorbing Layers.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Scattering Boundary Condition. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewte").create("sctr1", "Scattering", 2)

parameters.name: Incident electric field E0
parameters.description: Time-dependent incoming field (V/m); zero for a purely absorbing boundary.

tools.example: 1D-like slab test in 2D: Scattering Boundary Condition on the left with E0 = (0, 0, E_pulse(t)) and on the right with E0 = 0 to absorb the transmitted pulse.
tools.notes: Other boundary nodes of the interface: Electric Field, Magnetic Field, PEC, PMC, Surface Current Density, Lumped Port and (advanced) Flux/Source.

tools.name: Flux/Source (Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Advanced boundary condition that directly prescribes the tangential electric field E0 and tangential magnetic field H0 through the DG numerical flux, i.e. the most general inflow/outflow condition of the time-explicit formulation. It is useful for imposing a known time-domain field on a boundary, such as a field recorded from another simulation.
tools.usage: Show More Options > Advanced Physics Options, then Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Flux/Source. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewte").create("fls1", "Flux", 2)

parameters.name: Tangential electric field E0
parameters.description: V/m.

parameters.name: Tangential magnetic field H0
parameters.description: A/m.

tools.example: Replay a pulse captured on a plane: Flux/Source on the input face with E0 and H0 given by interpolation functions of (y, z, t) exported from an earlier model.
tools.notes: See 'Fluxes as Dirichlet Boundary Conditions' in the theory section of the RF Module User's Guide.

tools.name: Background Field (Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Domain feature that switches the time-explicit interface to the scattered-field formulation, E = E_relative + E_background, with a user-defined background (Eb, Hb, differentiable in time) or a built-in modulated Gaussian plane-wave pulse. The pulse has duration 1/(2*f0) and delay 2/f0 so it starts negligibly small, making it the standard illumination for wideband time-domain scattering and RCS.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Background Field (3D, 2D). API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewte").create("bf1", "BackgroundField", 3)

parameters.name: Background wave type
parameters.description: User defined (Eb, Hb) or Modulated Gaussian pulse.

parameters.name: Direction of propagation / Polarization direction
parameters.description: +-x, +-y, +-z and a transverse polarization axis.

parameters.name: Center frequency f0 / Phase velocity vp / Wave impedance Z
parameters.description: Defaults 1 GHz, c_const, Z0_const.

parameters.name: Distance from origin to wave launching plane
parameters.description: doffset, default 0 m.

tools.notes: Apply it to all domains outside and inside the scatterer except absorbing layers as appropriate; the relative field is what the absorbing layers must absorb.

tools.name: Far-Field Domain and Far-Field Calculation (Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Far-field transformation for the time-explicit interface: a Far-Field Domain (homogeneous region outside all scatterers) with a Far-Field Calculation subnode on a closed surface, including symmetry-plane settings (Symmetry in E (PMC) or Symmetry in H (PEC)) and inside/outside orientation. Because the transformation works on frequency-domain data, a Time to Frequency FFT study step must follow the Time Dependent step, after which radiation patterns and RCS are available at every FFT frequency.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Far-Field Domain (adds Far-Field Calculation); Study: Time Dependent + Time to Frequency FFT. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewte").create("ffd1", "FarFieldDomain", 3)

parameters.name: Far-field variable name
parameters.description: Default Efar.

parameters.name: Symmetry in the x=0, y=0, z=0 planes
parameters.description: Checkbox and type (PMC or PEC) per plane.

parameters.name: Boundary relative to domain
parameters.description: Outside (default) or Inside.

tools.notes: The Electromagnetic Waves, Transient interface also has a Far-Field Domain with the same FFT requirement.

tools.name: Absorbing Layer (Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Definitions-level domain feature (listed with the coordinate systems, like a PML) that turns a shell of elements around the model into a nonreflecting layer for the time-explicit DG interfaces, using a coordinate scaling that pushes energy into high polynomial modes which the DG filter then damps. It plays the role of the PML for the Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit interface.
tools.usage: Definitions toolbar > Absorbing Layer (or Coordinate Systems > Absorbing Layer; right-click Definitions > Absorbing Layer), select the layer domains; filter parameters in the interface's 'Filter Parameters for Absorbing Layers' section. Type string: AbsorbingLayer (default tag ab1).

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: Outer shell domains, preferably with a structured mesh.

parameters.name: Filter parameters (interface level)
parameters.description: alpha = 0.5, eta_c = 0.1, s = 4 by default; overly aggressive filtering causes spurious reflections.

tools.example:
Spherical air domain with an outer spherical shell: add Absorbing Layer 1 on the shell and keep Wave Equations filter settings Automatic.
Application Library: RF_Module/Scattering_and_RCS/rcs_time_explicit
tools.notes: Also used by other time-explicit wave interfaces (acoustics). For the implicit frequency- and time-domain interfaces use Perfectly Matched Layers instead.

tools.name: Lumped Port (Electromagnetic Waves, Transient and Time Explicit)
tools.description: Time-domain lumped port that drives or terminates a transmission-line-like gap with a voltage or current waveform. With 'Calculate S-parameter' the port is driven by a modulated Gaussian pulse (center frequency f0, small modulation upshift) so that a Time to Frequency FFT yields broadband S-parameters from one transient run; current-driven ports offer built-in electrostatic-discharge (human body, extended human body, machine, charged device model) and lightning pulses for EMC/ESD tests.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Transient (temw/ewt) or Time Explicit (ewte) > Boundaries > Lumped Port. API: model.component("comp1").physics("temw").create("lport1", "LumpedPort", 2); feature("lport1").set("CalcSparam", "1"); set("VoltageSourceType", "ModulatedGaussianPulse"); set("f0", "1[GHz]")

parameters.name: TerminalType
parameters.description: Cable (voltage, with Zref) or Current.

parameters.name: CalcSparam / VoltageSourceType / f0 / fmodShiftRatio
parameters.description: S-parameter mode with a modulated Gaussian pulse; upshift ratio default 3%.

parameters.name: V0 (User defined)
parameters.description: Arbitrary voltage waveform, e.g. an analytic trapezoid an1(t).

parameters.name: CurrentPulseType / ElectrostaticDischargePulseModel
parameters.description: UserDefined, ElectrostaticDischarge (HumanBodyModel ...) or Lightning; Plot Pulse Shape button.

tools.notes: In the frequency-domain emw interface S-parameters are computed automatically; in the transient interfaces the checkbox is required. Resolve the highest frequency of the pulse in both mesh and time step.

tools.name: Wave Equation, Electric (Electromagnetic Waves, Transient)
tools.description: Main domain node of the Electromagnetic Waves, Transient interfaces (temw, ewt), solving the time-domain wave equation for the magnetic vector potential. Besides relative permittivity and refractive index (real part only), it supports a Polarization P, a Remanent electric displacement Dr (used for nonlinear optics such as Dr = d33*Ez^2), and the Drude-Lorentz dispersion model realized by auxiliary polarization ODEs; magnetic options include relative permeability, remanent flux density, magnetization and a nonlinear B-H curve.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Transient > Wave Equation, Electric 1. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewt").feature("wee1").set("DisplacementFieldModel", "DrudeLorentzDispersionModel"); set("omegap", "omega_p"); set("epsilonInf", ...)

parameters.name: DisplacementFieldModel
parameters.description: RelativePermittivity (default), RefractiveIndex, Polarization (P), Remanent electric displacement (Dr), DrudeLorentzDispersionModel (epsilonInf, omegap).

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationH
parameters.description: RelativePermeability, Remanent flux density (Br), Magnetization (M) or B-H curve (normH).

parameters.name: Conduction current
parameters.description: sigma, linearized resistivity, effective medium or Archie's law.

tools.example:
Kerr-type nonlinearity in a Bragg stack: DisplacementFieldModel = Remanent electric displacement with Dr = (0, 0, d33*ewt.Ez^2) in the nonlinear layers.
Application Libraries: Wave_Optics_Module/Couplers_Filters_and_Mirrors/time_to_frequency_fft_distributed_bragg_reflector, RF_Module/Tutorials/drude_lorentz_media
tools.notes: Nonlinear B-H simulations may need BDF with a small constant maximum step and low maximum order (e.g. 2). A Divergence Constraint subnode stabilizes quasi-static regimes.

tools.name: Drude-Lorentz Polarization (Electromagnetic Waves, Transient)
tools.description: Subnode of Wave Equation, Electric (with the Drude-Lorentz dispersion model) that adds one polarization term P_n governed by a damped-oscillator ODE with oscillator strength f_n, resonance frequency omega_n and damping Gamma_n, driven by the plasma frequency omega_p of the parent. Several subnodes build a multi-pole fit of metal or dielectric dispersion for time-domain simulations of plasmonics and metamaterials.
tools.usage: Wave Equation, Electric (Drude-Lorentz dispersion model) > right-click > Drude-Lorentz Polarization. API: model.component("comp1").physics("temw").feature("wee2").create("dlp1", "DrudeLorentzPolarization", 2)

parameters.name: Oscillator strength f_n
parameters.description: Dimensionless.

parameters.name: Resonance frequency omega_n / Damping in time Gamma_n
parameters.description: rad/s; omega_n = 0 gives a Drude term.

parameters.name: Initial values P_n, dP_n/dt
parameters.description: Default zero.

parameters.name: Discretization (advanced)
parameters.description: Element order of P_n.

tools.notes: Each subnode adds vector DOFs; keep the number of poles small. The frequency-domain equivalent is the Drude-Lorentz dispersion model of Wave Equation, Electric in emw/ewfd.

tools.name: Scattering Boundary Condition (Electromagnetic Waves, Transient)
tools.description: Absorbing boundary of the vector-potential time-domain interfaces for plane, cylindrical or spherical outgoing waves that can also inject an incident field given as a time function E0i(t). An advanced 'Dispersion and absorption' setting chooses how the wave number and attenuation of the incident and scattered waves are evaluated in lossy media: Low loss approximation (default) or High loss with a carrier frequency.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Scattering Boundary Condition. API: model.component("comp1").physics("temw").create("sctr1", "Scattering", 2); feature("sctr1").set("IncidentField", "EField"); set("E0i", new String[]{"0", "E_pulse*E_bnd", "0"})

parameters.name: IncidentField / E0i / H0i
parameters.description: NoIncidentField or EField/HField with a time-dependent amplitude.

parameters.name: WaveType / kdir / r0 / raxis
parameters.description: Plane (default), cylindrical or spherical wave and its geometry.

parameters.name: Initial Values for Incident Wave (Ai0)
parameters.description: Initial magnetic vector potential of the incident wave.

parameters.name: DispersionAndAbsorptionModel / CarrierFrequency
parameters.description: LowLossApproximation (default) or high-loss model with carrier frequency (default 1 GHz).

tools.notes: Like its frequency-domain counterpart it is only perfectly absorbing at normal incidence; the frequency-domain SBC is catalogued generically as 'Scattering Boundary Condition'.

tools.name: Impedance Boundary Condition (Electromagnetic Waves, Transient)
tools.description: Time-domain version of the impedance boundary condition for exterior boundaries of good conductors. Because the surface admittance of a conductor is strongly frequency dependent, it is approximated by a partial-fraction fit over a user-specified frequency band and realized with auxiliary ODE variables on the boundary, which also makes it usable in eigenfrequency analyses. The approximation is computed as a preprocessing step and can be previewed.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Transient > Boundaries > Impedance Boundary Condition; Time Domain and Eigenfrequency section > Compute approximation / Preview plot. API: model.component("comp1").physics("temw").create("imp1", "Impedance", 2)

parameters.name: epsrb / murb / sigmab
parameters.description: Properties of the excluded conductor, From material by default.

parameters.name: Frequency range
parameters.description: Bandwidth and center (fc, decades nd) or Minimum and maximum (fmin, fmax).

parameters.name: Accuracy
parameters.description: Higher accuracy or wider band means more auxiliary variables.

parameters.name: Show approximation data
parameters.description: Inspect the fitted poles/residues; skin depth at fc is reported.

tools.example: Lossy-wall version of a transient coaxial low-pass filter (the Application Library model RF_Module/Filters/coaxial_low_pass_filter_transient uses PEC walls): replace PEC by an Impedance Boundary Condition on the copper walls, set Frequency range 0.1-10 GHz, click Compute approximation, then solve the Time Dependent study with the pulse on the lumped port and compare the insertion loss.
tools.notes: If the approximation is not computed manually it is computed automatically at the start of the solver, using the section's settings.

tools.name: Transition Boundary Condition (Electromagnetic Waves, Transient)
tools.description: Time-domain thin conductive layer on interior boundaries, with layer types Electrically very thin (tangential E continuous, low-frequency limit), Electrically thin (default) and Electrically thick (decoupled sides, equivalent to two impedance conditions). The frequency-dependent surface and transfer admittances are replaced by partial-fraction fits and auxiliary ODEs; for the thin and very thin types the fit is precomputed, while the thick type needs a user frequency range and approximation.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Transient > Boundaries > Transition Boundary Condition. API: model.component("comp1").physics("temw").create("trans1", "TransitionBoundaryCondition", 2)

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Electrically very thin layer, Electrically thin layer (default), Electrically thick layer.

parameters.name: epsrb / murb / sigmab / Surface thickness ds
parameters.description: Layer properties, From material by default.

parameters.name: Time Domain and Eigenfrequency (thick layer only)
parameters.description: Frequency range and accuracy of the admittance fit.

tools.example: Shielding effectiveness of a thin aluminum enclosure wall excited by an ESD pulse: Transition Boundary Condition (Electrically thin layer, ds = 0.5[mm]) on the enclosure faces in temw.
tools.notes: Assumes propagation normal to the layer and isotropic properties; thickness smaller than the radius of curvature.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Waves, Asymptotic Scattering (ewas)
tools.description: RF interface (type ElectromagneticWavesAsymptoticScattering) for very fast estimates of the far-field scattering of electrically large objects made of perfect electric conductors: an Asymptotic Scattering feature assigns a surface electric field derived from the background wave to the boundaries, and the Far-Field Calculation applies the Stratton-Chu formula in postprocessing - no volume mesh or matrix solve of the full-wave problem is needed. Supports 2D and 3D Frequency Domain studies with user-defined or linearly polarized plane-wave backgrounds.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Radio Frequency > Electromagnetic Waves, Asymptotic Scattering (ewas). API: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ewas", "ElectromagneticWavesAsymptoticScattering", "geom1")

parameters.name: Background wave type
parameters.description: User defined Eb, or (3D) Linearly polarized plane wave with amplitude, roll/pitch/yaw angles and wave number (default ewas.k0).

parameters.name: Asymptotic Scattering (default, type AsymptoticScattering)
parameters.description: Assigns the background field on adjacent boundaries.

parameters.name: Far-Field Calculation (default)
parameters.description: Far-field variable name Efar; operator orders in advanced settings.

parameters.name: Physics-controlled mesh
parameters.description: lambda0/5 on boundaries from the study frequency.

tools.example:
Scattering estimate for a metal sphere: ewas with a linearly polarized plane wave background, Frequency Domain sweep, then a Radiation Pattern plot of ewas.normdBEfar from the default Far-Field Calculation.
Application Library: RF_Module/Scattering_and_RCS/rcs_sphere_asymptotic
tools.notes: Only PEC objects are represented; multiple reflections, creeping waves and dielectrics are ignored (a physical-optics-type approximation). Verify with the full-wave or BEM interface for accuracy-critical results.

tools.name: Wave Equation, Electric (Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements)
tools.description: Domain node of the boundary-element interfaces (embe, ebem) that assigns the homogeneous material of each region, including the infinite void outside the geometry. Because BEM relies on the analytic Green's function, relative permittivity, relative permeability and conductivity must evaluate to constants in each Wave Equation, Electric node, so every different dielectric needs its own node; the full list of displacement field models (refractive index, loss tangent, Drude-Lorentz, Debye, wideband Debye) is available.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements > Wave Equation, Electric (domain selection may include voids: infinite void = entity 0, finite voids negative numbers). API: model.component("comp1").physics("ebem").create("wee2", "WaveEquationElectric", 3)

parameters.name: Electric displacement field model
parameters.description: As in emw, constant values only.

parameters.name: mur / sigma
parameters.description: From material or User defined constants.

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: Manual, All domains, All voids, All domains and voids (default).

tools.example:
Optical Yagi-Uda nanoantenna: Wave Equation, Electric 1 on the infinite void (air), Wave Equation, Electric 2 on the gold elements with Drude-Lorentz data, dipole background field.
Application Library: Wave_Optics_Module/Optical_Scattering/optical_yagi_uda_antenna
tools.notes: With several Wave Equation, Electric nodes, the infinite-void selection must belong to the first one. Graded or anisotropic media require FEM (couple through FEM-BEM).

tools.name: Far-Field Calculation (Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements)
tools.description: Far-field evaluation of the boundary-element interfaces: it selects all boundaries between the infinite void and radiating or scattering material domains, voids or surfaces, and generates the usual far-field variables (Efar components, normEfar, RCS, gain) directly from the BEM surface unknowns. Interior material boundaries are ignored automatically.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements > Far-Field Calculation. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ebem").create("ffc1", "FarFieldCalculation", 2)

parameters.name: Far-field variable name
parameters.description: Default Efar.

parameters.name: Advanced settings
parameters.description: Average operator integration order and maximum operator point type/order (default 2).

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ebem").create("ffc1", "FarFieldCalculation", 2);
// plot ebem.normEfar in a Radiation Pattern; Application Library: Wave_Optics_Module/Optical_Scattering/optical_yagi_uda_antenna
tools.notes: No far-field domain or PML is needed in BEM because the exterior is infinite by construction.

tools.name: Lumped Port (Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements)
tools.description: Lumped port of the RF boundary-element interface, of type Coaxial, User defined or Via, with a Cable terminal that excites (voltage with phase, or power) or terminates the device and yields S-parameters. Combined with the interface's Port Sweep Settings and Touchstone export it gives antenna-array coupling matrices computed with BEM surface meshes only.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements > Boundaries > Lumped Port. API: model.component("comp1").physics("embe").create("lport1", "LumpedPort", 2)

parameters.name: Type of lumped port
parameters.description: Coaxial, User defined (hPort, wPort, direction), Via.

parameters.name: Wave excitation / Source type
parameters.description: On/off; Voltage (V0, phase) or Power (P0).

parameters.name: Characteristic impedance Zref
parameters.description: Reference impedance.

tools.example:
Dipole antenna array coupling matrix with BEM: lumped ports at each feed gap, embe Port Sweep Settings > Use manual port sweep + Export Touchstone file.
Application Library: RF_Module/Antenna_Arrays/dipole_antenna_array
tools.notes: Only the Cable terminal type is available in embe.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements (ebem)
tools.description: Wave Optics Module version of the boundary-element Maxwell solver (type ElectromagneticWavesBEM, tag ebem) for piecewise-homogeneous optical problems such as nanoantennas, scatterer arrays and elements located many wavelengths apart, supporting Frequency Domain and Wavelength Domain studies. Its background-field options include plane waves, Gaussian beams and an electric point dipole source; a stabilized formulation and ACA-based far-field matrix compression keep large problems tractable.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Optics > Wave Optics > Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements (ebem). API: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ebem", "ElectromagneticWavesBEM", "geom1"); physics("ebem").prop("BackgroundField").set("SolveFor", "scatteredField"); prop("BackgroundField").set("WaveType", "ElectricPointDipole")

parameters.name: BackgroundField (SolveFor, WaveType)
parameters.description: Full or scattered field; user defined, Gaussian beam, linearly polarized plane wave or ElectricPointDipole (ElectricPointDipoleType, pQ, r0).

parameters.name: Stabilization
parameters.description: Use stabilization (on by default in the physics settings) with parameter sqrt(abs(ebem.k[m])) - benefits large models.

parameters.name: Far-Field Approximation / Quadrature
parameters.description: ACA+ matrix compression for assembly; minimum near-field range for preconditioning (default one tenth of a wavelength).

parameters.name: Symmetry
parameters.description: PEC or PMC symmetry planes normal to the axes at given coordinates.

tools.notes: Dense BEM matrices make each DOF more expensive than FEM; for small to medium problems ewfd is often faster. The RF counterpart is 'Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements (embe)'.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Waves, FEM-BEM (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface that adds an Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain interface (for inhomogeneous parts such as feeds, substrates and dielectric lenses) and an Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements interface (for the unbounded exterior), joined by an Electric Field Coupling that enforces continuity of the tangential electric field. The hybrid avoids large air domains and PMLs for radiators and scatterers in open space and is available in the RF (emw + embe) and Wave Optics (ewfd + ebem) modules.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Radio Frequency (or Wave Optics) > Electromagnetic Waves, FEM-BEM; or add both interfaces and Multiphysics > Electric Field Coupling. Supports Frequency Domain (and Wavelength Domain) studies in 2D and 3D.

parameters.name: Constituent interfaces
parameters.description: emw/ewfd on the meshed domains; embe/ebem on the exterior (void) and remaining homogeneous domains.

parameters.name: Coupling
parameters.description: Electric Field Coupling with boundary selection equal to the FEM domain boundaries.

parameters.name: Alternative
parameters.description: Use the same dependent-variable name in both interfaces instead of the coupling node.

tools.example:
Microstrip patch antenna: FEM for the substrate and patch region with a lumped port, BEM for the surrounding air; Far-Field Calculation in the BEM interface gives the pattern without a PML.
Application Library: RF_Module/Antennas/microstrip_patch_antenna_fem_bem
tools.notes: If the interfaces are added one at a time, the modified multiphysics settings are not included automatically.

tools.name: Electric Field Coupling (FEM-BEM multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling node (type ElectricFieldCoupling, tag elfc) that ties the tangential electric field of the finite-element Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain interface (primary) to that of the Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements interface (secondary) on the boundaries where the FEM region meets the BEM region. It is what turns two separate interfaces into a FEM-BEM model.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Multiphysics > Electric Field Coupling (boundary level). API: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("elfc1", "ElectricFieldCoupling", 2); multiphysics("elfc1").set("E_src_physics", "emw"); multiphysics("elfc1").set("E_dst_physics", "embe")

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Manual or All boundaries (exterior FEM boundaries touching the BEM region).

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Primary: Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain; Secondary: Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements.

tools.notes: Coupling property names follow COMSOL's <couplingtype>_physics convention (E_src/E_dst); check with Compact History if in doubt.

tools.name: Wave Equation, Beam Envelopes (Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes)
tools.description: Main domain node of the Beam Envelopes interface: the field is written E = E1*exp(-j*phi1) (+ E2*exp(-j*phi2) for bidirectional propagation) with a prescribed fast phase, and this node solves the resulting wave equation for the slowly varying envelopes E1 and E2. Its material settings are the same as Wave Equation, Electric (refractive index, loss models, dispersion, permeability, conductivity); in Eigenfrequency studies it also yields the Q factor.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes > Wave Equation, Beam Envelopes 1 (default, type WaveEquationBeamEnvelopes, tag webe). API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewbe").feature("webe1").set("DisplacementFieldModel", "RefractiveIndex")

parameters.name: Electric displacement field model
parameters.description: Same list as Wave Equation, Electric; RefractiveIndex is common in optics.

parameters.name: Magnetic field / Conduction current
parameters.description: mur (or magnetic losses) and sigma.

tools.example:
Polarizing beam splitter: Wave Equation, Beam Envelopes with refractive index from the Optical Material Library in each layer; bidirectional wave vectors handle the reflected beam.
Application Library: Wave_Optics_Module/Applications/polarizing_beam_splitter
tools.notes: Within a domain the two envelopes are not coupled unless weak expressions are added; coupling happens at boundaries.

tools.name: Wave Vectors and Phase Specification (Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes)
tools.description: Interface-level settings that define the prescribed fast phase of the Beam Envelopes interface: Unidirectional (one envelope) or Bidirectional (two envelopes, default) propagation, with phases given either by constant wave vectors k1, k2 (default k1 along x and k2 its mirror image) or by user-defined continuous phase functions phi1, phi2. The better the phase matches the real propagation, the coarser the mesh can be - often only a few elements per thousands of wavelengths along the beam - which is why the interface suits long waveguides, couplers, lenses and laser cavities.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes > Wave Vectors; User Defined Wave Vector Specification (for PMLs and user-defined phases). API: physics("ewbe").prop("WaveVector").set("dirCount", "UniDirectionality"); prop("WaveVector").set("PhaseSpec", "WaveVector"); prop("WaveVector").set("k1", new String[]{"ewbe.beta_1", "0", "0"}); prop("WaveVector").set("phase1", "phi1")

parameters.name: dirCount
parameters.description: BiDirectionality (default) or UniDirectionality.

parameters.name: PhaseSpec / k1, k2 / phase1, phase2
parameters.description: WaveVector (constant vectors) or UserDefined (continuous phase expressions).

parameters.name: UserDefinedWaveVectorSpecification (k1Phase, k2Phase)
parameters.description: Wave vectors for user-defined phases; set explicitly in PML domains.

parameters.name: MeshControl (MeshType, elemCountT, elemCountL, hMax)
parameters.description: Physics-controlled mesh: Swept (3D default)/Mapped (2D default) with 10 transverse and 10 longitudinal elements, or Tetrahedral/Triangular with a maximum size.

parameters.name: averagedLossCalculation
parameters.description: Drops E1-E2 cross terms from the loss (heat source) when the beating is not resolved.

tools.notes: The phase must be continuous across boundaries except at Transition, Layered Transition and Field Continuity boundaries (and material discontinuities in the bidirectional formulation). For strongly scattering problems the envelope oscillates rapidly and ewfd is the better choice.

tools.name: Matched Boundary Condition (Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes)
tools.description: Low-reflecting boundary of the Beam Envelopes interface that is transparent for waves having the phase prescribed in the Wave Vectors settings, even at large angles to the boundary normal, and that can launch an incident envelope given by E, H or a Gaussian beam (waist radius, focal distance, amplitude or power). In the bidirectional formulation it selects which wave (first or second) carries the input.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes > Boundaries > Matched Boundary Condition. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewbe").create("mbc1", "MatchedBoundaryCondition", 1); feature("mbc1").set("InputWave", "FirstWave"); set("IncidentField", "GaussianBeam"); set("inputQuantity", "Power")

parameters.name: InputWave
parameters.description: FirstWave (default) or SecondWave (bidirectional only).

parameters.name: IncidentField
parameters.description: NoIncidentField, EField, HField or GaussianBeam (w0, p0, Eg0 or inputPower).

parameters.name: Incident wave direction kdir
parameters.description: Needed for Gaussian beams with user-defined phase.

parameters.name: NoScatteredField
parameters.description: Suppress spurious solutions (bidirectional).

tools.notes: Only the envelope factor is entered; the phase function is multiplied in automatically.

tools.name: Field Continuity (Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes)
tools.description: Advanced interior-boundary condition for the unidirectional Beam Envelopes formulation that enforces continuity of the tangential electric and magnetic fields when the prescribed phase phi1 is discontinuous across the boundary. It lets different, locally better phase approximations be used in adjacent domains - for example a straight-waveguide phase next to a ring-resonator phase.
tools.usage: Show More Options > Advanced Physics Options; Boundaries > Field Continuity (unidirectional only). API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewbe").create("fcont1", "FieldContinuity", 1)

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Interior boundaries where the phase changes.

parameters.name: Constraint Settings
parameters.description: Advanced constraint options.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ewbe").create("fcont1", "FieldContinuity", 1);
// Application Libraries: Wave_Optics_Module/Couplers_Filters_and_Mirrors/optical_ring_resonator, optical_ring_resonator_3d
tools.notes: Do not use it between different materials; there reflections occur and the bidirectional formulation is more appropriate.

tools.name: Port (Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes)
tools.description: Port feature of the Beam Envelopes interface that excites and absorbs waveguide modes on input and output faces of long optical devices, most often of Numeric type with a Boundary Mode Analysis per port, or Periodic for unit cells. The computed propagation constants (ewbe.beta_1, ewbe.neff_1) are typically reused as the wave vectors of the envelope phase, and linear polarization for periodic ports is specified as S or P with a P-power fraction.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes > Boundaries > Port. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewbe").create("port1", "Port", 2); feature("port1").set("PortType", "Numeric"); set("PortExcitation", "on"); set("Pin", "Pin1")

parameters.name: PortType
parameters.description: Numeric (with Boundary Mode Analysis), Periodic and the other emw types.

parameters.name: PortExcitation / Pin / Thetap
parameters.description: Excitation, input power and mode phase (e.g. ph1 for coherent combining).

parameters.name: LinearPol / etaP (periodic)
parameters.description: S or P polarization and P-polarization power fraction.

parameters.name: Port Options (PortFormulation)
parameters.description: Weak (default) or constraint-based.

tools.example:
Directional coupler: four numeric ports, Boundary Mode Analysis steps for ports 1-4 (shift near the core index) followed by a Wavelength Domain step; plot abs(ewbe.S21)^2 and abs(ewbe.S31)^2.
Application Library: Wave_Optics_Module/Couplers_Filters_and_Mirrors/directional_coupler
tools.notes: S-parameters and Touchstone export work as in emw (ewbe.S11, ewbe.S21).

tools.name: Polarization (Electromagnetic Waves domain source for nonlinear optics)
tools.description: Domain node of the Wave Optics frequency-domain and beam-envelope interfaces that adds an externally generated polarization P_i to the total polarization, P = eps0*(epsr-1)*E + sum P_i. It is the standard way to couple two frequency-domain interfaces at different frequencies, e.g. a second-harmonic source P(2w) = 2*d*E(w)*E(w) in the interface solved at 2w, or to represent any known induced dipole density.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Polarization (ewfd, ewbe). API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewfd2").create("pol1", "Polarization", 2); feature("pol1").set("P", new String[]{"0", "d*ewfd1.Ey*ewfd1.Ey", "0"})

parameters.name: Polarization P
parameters.description: Vector in C/m^2.

parameters.name: Polarization, first/second wave P1, P2 (ewbe bidirectional)
parameters.description: One polarization per envelope.

tools.example:
Second-harmonic generation: ewfd1 solved at f (EquationForm freq_src userdef, freq = f), ewfd2 at 2f with Polarization P = (0, d*ewfd1.Ey*ewfd1.Ey, 0) in the nonlinear crystal.
Application Library: Wave_Optics_Module/Verification_Examples/second_harmonic_generation_frequency_domain
tools.notes: For each interface set its own frequency in Equation Form (form Frequency, freq_src userdef). Strongly nonlinear or broadband problems belong in the time domain (ewt).

tools.name: Cross Section Calculation (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Wave Optics domain feature that computes the scattering, absorption and extinction cross sections of a scatterer in a scattered-field model: sigma_sca from the scattered Poynting flux through a surface enclosing the particle, sigma_abs from the volume-integrated loss density, sigma_ext = sigma_sca + sigma_abs, all normalized by the incident intensity. Results appear as global variables ewfd.sigmaSca, ewfd.sigmaAbs and ewfd.sigmaExt, e.g. for Mie-type nanoparticle spectra.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Cross Section Calculation (select the whole scatterer). API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewfd").create("csc1", "CrossSectionCalculation", 3); feature("csc1").set("I0", "0.5*(1[V/m])^2/Z0_const")

parameters.name: Incident plane wave intensity I0
parameters.description: Needed for a User defined background (default 1 W/m^2); computed automatically for built-in plane waves.

tools.notes: Only available with Formulation = Scattered field and background types User defined (2D), User defined or circularly polarized plane wave (2D-axi), User defined or linearly polarized plane wave (3D).

tools.name: Laser Heating (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface (Wave Optics + heat transfer) that adds Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes, Heat Transfer in Solids and an Electromagnetic Heating coupling, so optical absorption of a laser beam becomes a heat source and temperature-dependent optical properties feed back. Because the beam-envelope formulation needs no wavelength-scale mesh along the beam, it handles millimeter-to-centimeter optical paths; studies are Frequency-Stationary and Frequency-Transient, or their one-way variants when optics does not depend on temperature.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Electromagnetic Heating > Laser Heating. API (manual assembly): physics().create("ewbe", "ElectromagneticWavesBeamEnvelopes", "geom1"); physics().create("ht", "HeatTransfer", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("emh1", "ElectromagneticHeating", 3); multiphysics("emh1").set("EMHeat_physics", "ewbe"); multiphysics("emh1").set("Heat_physics", "ht")

parameters.name: Electromagnetic Heating (emh1)
parameters.description: Domain and boundary heat sources from resistive/dielectric and surface losses.

parameters.name: averagedLossCalculation (ewbe)
parameters.description: Remove E1-E2 interference from the heat source when the beating is unresolved.

parameters.name: Studies
parameters.description: Frequency-Stationary, Frequency-Transient, and One-Way Electromagnetic Heating variants.

tools.example:
SESAM mirror heated by a pump laser: Laser Heating interface, Gaussian beam via Matched/Scattering boundary on ewbe, Frequency-Stationary study, then plot temperature and ewbe.nPoav.
Application Library: Wave_Optics_Module/Couplers_Filters_and_Mirrors/sesam_laser_heating
tools.notes: If ewbe and ht are added separately, add the coupling before adding the study so the Frequency-Stationary/Transient studies are offered. For geometric-optics-scale beams use Ray Heating instead.

tools.name: Microwave Heating (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface of the RF Module that adds Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain, Heat Transfer in Solids and the Electromagnetic Heating coupling (tag emh1). The coupling maps resistive plus magnetic loss densities (and surface losses of impedance boundaries) into the heat equation, and temperature can drive the electromagnetic material properties, for devices from about a tenth of a wavelength up to tens of wavelengths: microwave ovens, RF ablation probes, industrial dryers and MRI implant heating.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Electromagnetic Heating > Microwave Heating. API: multiphysics().create("emh1", "ElectromagneticHeating", 3); multiphysics("emh1").set("EMHeat_physics", "emw"); multiphysics("emh1").set("Heat_physics", "ht"); multiphysics("emh1").selection().all()

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces (EMHeat_physics, Heat_physics)
parameters.description: Electromagnetic and heat transfer interfaces.

parameters.name: Domain / Boundary selection
parameters.description: Where the volumetric and boundary electromagnetic heat sources apply.

parameters.name: Studies
parameters.description: Frequency-Stationary, Frequency-Transient, Frequency-Stationary/Transient One-Way Electromagnetic Heating.

tools.notes: Assumes the electromagnetic period is much shorter than thermal time scales. The generic 'Electromagnetic Heating / Joule Heating' entry covers the coupling concept across modules.

tools.name: Frequency-Stationary and Frequency-Transient Studies (Microwave and Laser Heating)
tools.description: Coupled study steps for electromagnetic heating: Frequency-Stationary (type FrequencyStationary) solves the frequency-domain wave problem and the stationary heat equation together until thermal equilibrium, while Frequency-Transient (type FrequencyTransient) marches the heat equation in time and re-solves the time-harmonic field whenever temperature-dependent properties change. Both apply to Microwave Heating, Laser Heating and Induction Heating, with the electromagnetic frequency given in the step.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies for Selected Multiphysics > Frequency-Stationary / Frequency-Transient. API: model.study("std1").create("fstat", "FrequencyStationary"); model.study("std1").feature("fstat").set("freq", "f0"); model.study("std1").create("ftrans", "FrequencyTransient"); model.study("std1").feature("ftrans").set("tlist", "range(0,15,300)")

parameters.name: freq
parameters.description: Electromagnetic frequency of the time-harmonic part.

parameters.name: tlist / initialtime (Frequency-Transient)
parameters.description: Output times of the thermal transient.

parameters.name: rtol / usertol
parameters.description: Tolerance control.

tools.notes: These studies only appear after the Electromagnetic Heating coupling exists. Other interfaces that support frequency studies (e.g. Solid Mechanics) should be set to a stationary equation form when included.

tools.name: One-Way Electromagnetic Heating Studies (Frequency-Stationary / Frequency-Transient, One-Way)
tools.description: Sequential preset studies for electromagnetic heating when the electromagnetic problem does not depend on temperature: a Frequency Domain step computes the field and loss once, then a Stationary or Time Dependent heat-transfer step uses the electromagnetic heat source. They are much cheaper than the fully coupled Frequency-Stationary/Transient studies and are available for Microwave Heating, Laser Heating and Induction Heating.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies for Selected Multiphysics > Frequency-Stationary, One-Way Electromagnetic Heating / Frequency-Transient, One-Way Electromagnetic Heating (creates Frequency Domain + Stationary or Time Dependent steps).

parameters.name: Step 1: Frequency Domain
parameters.description: Solves the electromagnetic interface only.

parameters.name: Step 2: Stationary / Time Dependent
parameters.description: Solves heat transfer with the stored electromagnetic solution as input.

tools.example: Pump laser heating a crystal with temperature-independent absorption: choose Frequency-Transient, One-Way Electromagnetic Heating and set the Time Dependent step to range(0,0.1,10) s.
tools.notes: If material properties (sigma, epsr, n) depend on T, use the fully coupled studies instead.

tools.name: Wavelength Domain (study)
tools.description: Wave Optics study step (type Wavelength) that sweeps the vacuum wavelength instead of the frequency for the Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain, Beam Envelopes and Boundary Elements interfaces, giving transmission, reflection and scattering spectra directly versus wavelength. It provides the frequency f = c0/lambda to all interfaces, supports auxiliary parameter sweeps (e.g. wavelength x angle) and can switch to the asymptotic waveform evaluation solver.
tools.usage: Add Study > Wavelength Domain (Wave Optics Module). API: model.study("std1").create("wave", "Wavelength"); model.study("std1").feature("wave").set("plist", "range(500[nm],10[nm],5[um])"); set("punit", "nm"); set("useparam", true); setIndex("pname_aux", "a", 0)

parameters.name: plist / punit
parameters.description: Vacuum wavelengths and unit (default um).

parameters.name: Tolerance / Reuse solution from previous step
parameters.description: Physics controlled or user relative tolerance.

parameters.name: Auxiliary sweep (useparam, pname_aux, plistarr_aux)
parameters.description: Multiparameter sweep with optional continuation.

parameters.name: Use asymptotic waveform evaluation
parameters.description: Replace the parametric solver by an AWE solver.

tools.notes: Requires the Wave Optics Module. Material data as functions of wavelength (lambda0) are evaluated at each step; mesh for the shortest wavelength.

tools.name: Thermal Lensing and STOP Analysis Workflow (Ray Heat Source with Bidirectionally Coupled Ray Tracing)
tools.description: Workflow for thermally induced focal shift (thermal lensing) and structural-thermal-optical performance (STOP) analysis: Geometrical Optics computes ray power, a Ray Heat Source multiphysics coupling deposits the power lost in absorbing glass into Heat Transfer in Solids, the temperature changes the refractive index through a thermo-optic model (Schott thermo-optic or Temperature-dependent Sellmeier), and optionally Thermal Expansion with Solid Mechanics deforms the lenses. The Bidirectionally Coupled Ray Tracing study alternates ray tracing and stationary thermal/structural solves for a set number of iterations until self-consistent.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Optics > Ray Optics > Ray Heating (+ Solid Mechanics and Thermal Expansion for STOP); Geometrical Optics > Intensity computation = Compute intensity and power; Study > Bidirectionally Coupled Ray Tracing. API: multiphysics().create("rhs1", "RayHeatSource", 3); multiphysics("rhs1").set("RayHeatSource_physics", "gop"); multiphysics("rhs1").set("RayHeatDestination_physics", "ht"); model.study("std1").create("bcrt", "BidirectionallyCoupledRayTracing"); feature("bcrt").set("iter", 5)

parameters.name: Ray Heat Source coupling
parameters.description: Source (gop) and destination (ht) interfaces; ray power must be solved for.

parameters.name: Medium Properties thermo-optic model
parameters.description: Schott thermo-optic coefficients or Temperature-dependent Sellmeier from the Optical Material Library.

parameters.name: Bidirectionally Coupled Ray Tracing: iter, timestepspec, llist, lunit
parameters.description: Number of iterations (default 5) and path-length based time stepping.

parameters.name: geometricNonlinearity
parameters.description: Include geometric nonlinearity so rays see the deformed geometry.

tools.notes: If rays do not change the temperature appreciably, a Stationary step followed by a plain Ray Tracing step is cheaper. The Ray Heating interface and Ray Tracing studies are catalogued generically elsewhere.

tools.name: Transmission Line Equation (Transmission Line interface)
tools.description: Main feature of the Transmission Line (tl) interface, defining the 1D telegrapher's wave equation for the line voltage V on domains (1D), boundaries (2D) or edges (3D) from distributed resistance R, inductance L, conductance G and capacitance C per unit length. The defaults (R = 0, L = 2.5e-6 H/m, G = 0, C = 1e-9 F/m) give a 50 ohm lossless line; with several signal conductors (up to 4) each quantity becomes a matrix to model coupled multiconductor lines.
tools.usage: Transmission Line > Transmission Line Equation 1 (default). API: model.component("comp1").physics("tl").create("tle2", "TransmissionLineEquation", 1); feature("tle2").set("L", "L0*z1"); set("C", "C0/z1")

parameters.name: R, L, G, C
parameters.description: Distributed parameters (ohm/m, H/m, S/m, F/m); matrices R2..R4 etc. for 2-4 lines.

parameters.name: Number of signal conductor lines (interface)
parameters.description: 1-4 electric-potential dependent variables.

parameters.name: Physics-controlled mesh
parameters.description: Maximum size 1/60 of the line wavelength at the highest study frequency.

tools.example:
Butler matrix built from ideal lines of different impedances: one Transmission Line Equation per impedance with L = L0*z and C = C0/z; Lumped Ports at the ends and a port sweep.
Application Libraries: RF_Module/Couplers_and_Power_Dividers/transmission_line_butler, RF_Module/Transmission_Lines_and_Waveguides/quarter_wave_transformer
tools.notes: Only the quasi-TEM mode is represented; get R, L, G, C for a real cross section from the Transmission Line, Parameters interface or a 2D mode analysis.

tools.name: Absorbing Boundary and Incoming Wave (Transmission Line)
tools.description: End conditions of the frequency-domain Transmission Line interface: Absorbing Boundary terminates the line in its characteristic impedance Z0 = sqrt((R + j*omega*L)/(G + j*omega*C)) so no wave is reflected, and Incoming Wave launches a wave of complex amplitude V0 (default 1 V) into the line while absorbing the reflected part. In the Transmission Line, Transient interface the incoming wave is sinusoidal (frequency and amplitude) or user defined in time.
tools.usage: Transmission Line > Boundaries (points) > Absorbing Boundary / Incoming Wave. API: model.component("comp1").physics("tl").create("ab1", "AbsorbingBoundary", 0); physics("tl").create("iw1", "IncomingWave", 0)

parameters.name: Electric potential V0 (Incoming Wave)
parameters.description: Complex amplitude, default 1 V.

parameters.name: Active line (multiconductor)
parameters.description: Signal line to which the condition applies.

tools.notes: Only on exterior boundaries (line ends). Use Lumped Port when S-parameters are required.

tools.name: Open Circuit, Short Circuit and Terminating Impedance (Transmission Line)
tools.description: Line-end conditions of the Transmission Line interfaces: Terminating Impedance loads the line with ZL (default 50 ohm), Open Circuit (the default end condition) is the ZL -> infinity case with zero current, and Short Circuit constrains V = 0. They model stubs, resonators and mismatched loads in distributed-element circuits.
tools.usage: Transmission Line > Boundaries (points) > Open Circuit / Short Circuit / Terminating Impedance. API: physics("tl").create("oc1", "OpenCircuit", 0); physics("tl").create("sc1", "ShortCircuit", 0); physics("tl").create("ti1", "TerminatingImpedance", 0)

parameters.name: Impedance ZL (Terminating Impedance)
parameters.description: Complex load impedance, default 50 ohm.

parameters.name: Active line
parameters.description: For multiconductor lines.

tools.example:
Quarter-wave shorted stub filter: Short Circuit at the stub end, Terminating Impedance 50 ohm at the output, Lumped Port at the input; sweep frequency and plot tl.S21dB.
Application Library: RF_Module/Filters/transmission_line_lpf
tools.notes: The Absorbing Boundary is the special case ZL = Z0. Short Circuit is allowed on interior points too.

tools.name: Lumped Port (Transmission Line)
tools.description: Point feature of the Transmission Line interface that excites or terminates a line and defines S-parameters (tl.S11, tl.S21dB), with port types Cable (reference impedance Zref, optional voltage excitation V0 with phase), Current (terminal current I0) and Circuit (connection to an Electrical Circuit). With the interface's port sweep it produces the full S-matrix of distributed networks and exports Touchstone files.
tools.usage: Transmission Line > Points > Lumped Port. API: model.component("comp1").physics("tl").create("lport1", "LumpedPort", 0); feature("lport1").set("PortName", "1"); set("TerminalType", "Cable"); set("PortExcitation", "on"); set("Zref", "50[ohm]")

parameters.name: PortName
parameters.description: Numeric name recommended (sweeps, Touchstone).

parameters.name: TerminalType
parameters.description: Cable (default), Current or Circuit.

parameters.name: V0 / Thetap / I0
parameters.description: Excitation voltage and phase (Cable) or current (Current).

parameters.name: activeLine
parameters.description: Signal line for multiconductor models.

tools.notes: The transient version (Transmission Line, Transient) drives the port with a sinusoidal or user-defined Vin(t) and has no S-parameters.

tools.name: Series Element and Shunt Element (Transmission Line)
tools.description: Interior point features of the Transmission Line interface that insert a lumped component in series with the line or in shunt to ground at a junction: a user-defined impedance or an inductor, capacitor, parallel/series LC or parallel/series RLC. They let lumped-distributed circuits such as matching networks and lumped low-pass filters be modelled without a separate circuit interface.
tools.usage: Transmission Line > Points > Series Element / Shunt Element. API: physics("tl").create("see1", "SeriesElement", 0); physics("tl").create("she1", "ShuntElement", 0)

parameters.name: Series/Shunt element device
parameters.description: User defined (Zelement, default 50 ohm), Inductor, Capacitor, Parallel LC, Series LC, Parallel RLC, Series RLC.

parameters.name: Lelement / Celement / Relement
parameters.description: Defaults 1 nH, 1 pF, 50 ohm.

parameters.name: Active line
parameters.description: For multiconductor lines.

tools.example: L-section matching network: Series Element (Inductor, 3.9 nH) followed by Shunt Element (Capacitor, 1.5 pF) between a 50 ohm feed line and a load represented by Terminating Impedance.
tools.notes: Only in the frequency-domain Transmission Line interface.

tools.name: Transmission Line, Transient (tlt)
tools.description: Time-domain version of the Transmission Line interface (type TransmissionLineTransient, tag tlt) solving the telegrapher's equation for the line voltage with a Time Dependent study in 1D, 2D and 3D. It is used for pulse propagation, reflections and ringing on cables and interconnects (TDR-type analyses) where a lumped-distributed line model is sufficient; features are Transmission Line Equation, Absorbing Boundary, Incoming Wave (sinusoidal or user defined), Open/Short Circuit, Terminating Impedance and Lumped Port.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Radio Frequency > Transmission Line, Transient (tlt). API: model.component("comp1").physics().create("tlt", "TransmissionLineTransient", "geom1"); model.study("std1").create("time", "Transient")

parameters.name: R, L, G, C
parameters.description: Distributed parameters (same defaults as tl).

parameters.name: Initial Values
parameters.description: V and dV/dt.

parameters.name: Incoming Wave / Lumped Port source
parameters.description: Sinusoidal (f0 = 1 GHz, amplitude 1 V) or user-defined Vin(t).

parameters.name: Physics-controlled mesh
parameters.description: User defined size, frequency or wavelength based (1/60 of the line wavelength).

tools.example: Step response of an unterminated 1 m cable: 1D tlt model with Lumped Port (User defined Vin = 1[V]*(t>0), Zref 50 ohm) at x = 0, Open Circuit at x = 1 m, Time Dependent study to 50 ns; plot V at both ends.
tools.notes: For multi-mode or radiating structures use Electromagnetic Waves, Transient or Time Explicit.

tools.name: Transmission Line, Parameters (tlpa)
tools.description: 2D frequency-domain interface (type TransmissionLineParameters, tag tlpa) that computes the per-unit-length series resistance R, series inductance L, shunt conductance G and shunt capacitance C of a two-conductor line cross section, plus its characteristic impedance Zc and propagation constant gamma. It solves for the electric potential V and the out-of-plane magnetic vector potential A with Dielectric, Free Space, Reference Conductor, Signal Conductor and Insulation features, and its physics-controlled mesh adds boundary layers resolving the skin depth in the conductors.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Radio Frequency > Transmission Line, Parameters (2D only). API: model.component("comp1").physics().create("tlpa", "TransmissionLineParameters", "geom1"); physics("tlpa").create("diel1", "Dielectric", 2); physics("tlpa").create("fsp1", "FreeSpace", 2)

parameters.name: Dielectric (diel)
parameters.description: Relative permittivity or loss-tangent models, From material by default.

parameters.name: Free Space (fsp)
parameters.description: Surrounding air with mur = 1 (Magnetic Flux Conservation).

parameters.name: Reference Conductor (refcnd) / Signal Conductor (scnd)
parameters.description: Conductor domains with electric conductivity.

parameters.name: Insulation (ins)
parameters.description: Default exterior condition (electric insulation, zero tangential A).

tools.example:
Coaxial cable parameters versus frequency: 2D cross section with Signal Conductor (inner), Reference Conductor (outer), Dielectric (PTFE); Frequency Domain sweep; evaluate R, L, G, C, Zc and use them in a tl model.
Application Library: RF_Module/Transmission_Lines_and_Waveguides/transmission_line_coaxial
tools.notes: Assumes a TEM mode and neglects conductive losses in the dielectric (G is due to dielectric loss only). A multiphysics coupling of the same name (tlp) also exists for series/shunt parameter analyses.

tools.name: Signal Conductor and Reference Conductor (Transmission Line, Parameters)
tools.description: Conductor domain features of the Transmission Line, Parameters interface. The Signal Conductor imposes 1 V (through a weak constraint with the surface charge density as Lagrange multiplier) and a 1 A current, from which the per-unit-length inductance, capacitance and conductance follow; the Reference Conductor fixes 0 V and returns its own resistance, so R = R_ref + R_sign. Together they define the two-conductor line whose parameters are extracted.
tools.usage: Transmission Line, Parameters > Signal Conductor / Reference Conductor (default nodes). API: physics("tlpa").create("scnd1", "SignalConductor", 2); physics("tlpa").create("refcnd1", "ReferenceConductor", 2)

parameters.name: Electric conductivity sigma
parameters.description: From material by default, or User defined.

tools.example: Microstrip on FR-4: Signal Conductor = copper trace domain, Reference Conductor = ground plane domain, Dielectric = substrate, Free Space = air box; sweep 1 MHz-10 GHz to see R rise with the skin effect.
tools.notes: L is the imaginary part of the total impedance over omega; C and G come from the real and imaginary parts of the charge/potential ratio.
